questions.prompt: Who created Hexagonal Architecture, and what is its other name?
questions.explanation: Alistair Cockburn introduced Hexagonal Architecture, also called Ports and Adapters. It is related to, but distinct from, Clean and Onion.

questions.prompt: Which of these are PRIMARY (driving) adapters — actors that call INTO the application? Select all that apply.

options.text: A web controller handling an HTTP request
An automated test driving a port
The database the application writes to

questions.explanation: Driving/primary adapters initiate action and call into the app (web, CLI, tests). The database is driven by the app, so it is a secondary/driven adapter.

questions.prompt: A ______ is an interface the application owns; an adapter is an implementation that connects it to a specific technology.
questions.explanation: Ports are the application-owned interfaces; adapters plug into them from the outside.

questions.prompt: What does the hexagon's six-sided shape signify?

options.text: Nothing special — it's just room to draw multiple ports on different edges

questions.explanation: Cockburn chose a hexagon only to leave room for several ports and to break the top-to-bottom 'layers' picture. The six sides carry no technical meaning.

questions.prompt: Map Hexagonal concepts to their Clean Architecture counterparts.
questions.explanation: The two approaches map closely, though they are distinct works; Clean Architecture adds explicit layering and component principles.

questions.prompt: Order the flow for a request in a ports-and-adapters system.
questions.explanation: A driving adapter calls a driving port into the app; the app calls out through a driven port to a driven adapter. Both sides use the same ports-and-adapters mechanism.
